answer.reason: The wrapper is meant to block only new work once the attempt is left, and stay transparent otherwise. If capabilities returns None, an attempt run under an attempt timeout no longer sees its provider's capabilities, so capability-dependent steps of that attempt can break or behave differently. This changes what the caller gets back from the route, which this requirement covers.

answer.finding: _LeftAttemptAdapter.aexecute is meant to forward async provider requests. Async attempts are cancelled when they time out, so no left attempt ever calls it, and replacing it with `return None` changes nothing a caller can observe.
answer.reason: The async method on the left-attempt adapter is only a pass-through, because async attempts are cancelled at their timeout. No left async attempt goes on to call it, and no test of the requirement, sync or async, runs it. Even if one did reach it, the original would send the very request the requirement forbids, so the mutant can't break the requirement.
